function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Sure! Those coordinates point right at **Google’s headquarters** – the “Googleplex” in Mountain View, California. | Coordinate | Approximate Street‑Level Address | |------------|----------------------------------| | `lat ≈ 37.4224764`

USA** | --- ### How to get this yourself programmatically Below is a quick example using two popular free services: #### 1️⃣ OpenStreetMap / Nominatim (no API key required) ```python import requests def reverse_geocode(lat, lon): url = "https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse" params = { "format": "json", "lat": lat, "lon": lon, "zoom": 18, # street-level detail "addressdetails": 1 # return structured components } headers = {"User-Agent": "MyApp/1.0 (+http://example.com)"} resp = requests.get(url, params=params, headers=headers) resp.raise_for_status() data = resp.json() print("Display Name:", data["display_name"]) if "address" in data: addr = data["address"] print("\nStructured Components:") for k,v in addr.items(): print(f"{k.title()}: {v}") reverse_geocode(37.4224764, -122.0842499) ``` *Result will show something along the lines of:* ``` Display Name: 1600, Amphitheatre Parkway, Charleston Road, ... , Mountain View, Santa Clara County, California, 94043, United States Address Details: Road: Amphitheatre Parkway City: Mountain View County: Santa Clara County State: California Postcode: 94043 Country: United States ... ``` #### 2️⃣ Google Maps Geocoding API (requires billing & API key) If you already have a Google Cloud project set up: ```bash curl \ "https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&key=YOUR_API_KEY" ``` or in Python: ```python from urllib.parse import urlencode import requests API_KEY = "YOUR_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY" payload = { "latlng": f"{37.4224764},{-122.0842499}", "key": API_KEY } resp = requests.get( "https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json", params=urlencode(payload), timeout=5 ) print(resp.json()["results"][0]["formatted_address"]) # -> 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA ``` --- ### Quick Summary - **Latitude:** 37.4224764 - **Longitude:** -122.0842499 - **Typical Reverse‑Geocoded Address:** *1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA* Feel free to plug those numbers into whichever reverse‑geocoding provider works best for your stack!
